Introduction:
**1:** Both sections cover the same core ideas: the 70%/25% dark energy/dark matter breakdown, the explanation that "dark" means invisible (no emission/reflection/absorption of light, impossible to observe directly), the default view of dark energy and dark matter as separate entities linked only by shared elusiveness, the 2024/2025 DESI findings that dark energy's strength is not constant, the ~2-billion-year-ago peak followed by weakening, the earlier-era stronger-and-defying-conservation finding, the phantom-regime/ball-rolling-uphill analogy requiring an external force, the growing theorist interest in a dark-matter tie, and the Tait quote framing a possible unified dark-sector theory. The generated section adds a guideline-required 5% ordinary-matter contrast, names Lambda-CDM explicitly, and appends the guideline's own Section 2 transition sentence verbatim — all additions, which do not count against completeness. No GT idea is absent.

Dark Interactions:
**1:** Both sections cover the same six substantive points and their attributed quotes: the 2005 Khoury et al. model (with Khoury's "most natural, simplest way" quote), the Khoury-Lin-Trodden dark-sector QCD analogue in which dark energy density and dark matter mass evolve together, the January 2025 model in which dark matter transfers energy to dark energy (with Teixeira's "brake" quote), Andriot's bookkeeping argument (with his "put into the box of dark energy" quote), Vafa's critique that dark energy cannot be computed independently of dark matter (with his quote), and the Hubble tension resolution via dark-sector interaction (including the ~9% figure and the Teixeira-et-al. "heated debates" quote). The generated section adds a brief QCD gloss ("the theory governing quarks and gluons") and expands on Andriot's mechanism with an accurate "secretly receiving two contributions" explanation; both are additions that do not displace any expected idea.

A Dark Dimension:
**0:** Most of the section's substance matches: the string-theory framework as a shared-origin candidate, the micron-scale dark dimension proposal, the graviton-leaks-into-the-dimension/dark-graviton mechanism, the natural coupling between dark-energy density (volume-dependent) and dark-matter mass (radius-dependent) with Obied's quote, the July 2025 Obied-Vafa-Bedroya-Wu predictions and Vafa's "won't change fast"/"entire age of the universe" quotes, the resulting long-range force and Obied's testability quote, the Kamionkowski-Kesden 2006 tidal-tail bound and Kamionkowski's quote, the testability-without-validation point, and the closing Obied quote on exploring the dark sector from multiple directions. However, the expected section's distinct 2019 finding — that Vafa and two collaborators, building on string theory's naturally varying dark energy, concluded the mass of dark matter particles may also vary over time (via moduli fields), which is what motivated the 2022 dark-dimension proposal — is entirely absent from the generated section. The generated section jumps directly from 'a common origin' to 'Vafa and his collaborators proposed... a dark dimension,' skipping this intermediate 2019 result. This is a substantive idea present in the expected section with no counterpart in the generated section. (The expected section's 'six or seven extra dimensions' figure is also dropped in favor of an unspecified 'extra dimensions,' a smaller factual-detail loss noted here for completeness but not independently decisive.) RE-EXAMINED on review against the standard since applied to similar cases in other replicates of this article (where an alternative-but-coherent derivation, e.g. via the Distance Conjecture, was found to preserve the same interdependence GT relies on and was not penalized): this section does not qualify for that same leniency. There, the generated text substituted a different but complete logical chain (tiny dark energy value → some consequence → shared origin). Here, there is no substitute reasoning at all — "Building on this" refers back only to "string theory... provides a potential framework," with no mention of varying dark matter mass, moduli fields, or any other bridge, before jumping straight to the dark-dimension proposal. This is a genuine gap, not an alternative path, so the 0 score is confirmed rather than revised.
